summary: Postinstall native dropper decrypts and executes staged ELF payload with sandbox evasion
details: The package's postinstall script auto-loads a bundled native addon (addon.node) and invokes its init() export. The addon reads an opaque 4.2 MB sibling file named.napi_cache (no printable strings at length >= 8, consistent with an encrypted/packed payload), writes the decoded bytes to /tmp/.<pid>, chmods the file, and uses fork/setsid/execlp to detach and execute it. Before executing, the addon runs an extensive environment-evasion gate: it checks for approximately twenty CI provider environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER, SANDBOX), container indicators via /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/1/cmdline, /proc/meminfo and /proc/cpuinfo (docker, containerd, kubepod, podman, dockerinit), and debugger presence via /proc/self/status TracerPid — detonating only on hosts that do not look like CI, containers, sandboxes, or analysis environments. The package ships no source, no build system, and no documentation justifying any of this behavior; its advertised purpose is a 'cache helper'. Installing this package on a non-sandboxed Linux host runs attacker-controlled native code with the installer's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
